o1.biggest_strength: Directly links operational decisions to the customer personas by protecting bridal artists like Farah with pro pre-orders and capping retail quantities during the stock crunch.
o1.biggest_mistake: Assumes the 6,400 held units are already inside the 9,100 on-hand count rather than additive (which would have completely eliminated the stockout gap to 8 December), though it transparently states this assumption.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Recognize that adding 3,900 held units to 9,100 on-hand gives 13,000 units (~3.4 weeks), bridging almost the entire gap until rush stock lands on 7 December.

o2.biggest_strength: The 'Night-out kit' bundling the two slowest-moving lines (liquid lipstick and glitter palette) together with explicit margin math is a brilliant commercial solution.
o2.biggest_mistake: Completely ignores the bridal makeup artist persona (Farah) who buys 6–10 units at once and risks clearing out remaining stock before regular shoppers get any.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Incorporate order quantity controls or bridal pre-allocations so large kit buyers don't instantly wipe out shade availability.

reason: Both plans are top-tier inventory models that stay strictly within the ₹1.2 crore budget, but Output 1 wins because it designs for my actual customers—capping consumer cart limits while creating a dedicated pro pre-order channel so bridal artists like Farah don't abandon the brand.
